items.title: Anonymous by contract? Applying the EDPB anonymisation flowchart to the DMA's Article 6(11) search-data measures
items.description: In July 2026 the EDPB adopted draft Guidelines 02/2026 on anonymisation, and nine days later the European Commission adopted its final measures in case DMA.100209, requiring Alphabet to share record-level Google Search data with rival search engines and calling the result anonymised. This paper tests that claim against the EDPB's own flowchart.

rssMetadata.excerpt: The Commission calls the Google Search data that Alphabet must share under DMA Article 6(11) anonymised. This paper tests that claim against the EDPB's July 2026 anonymisation flowchart.

items.title: CPDP 2026: The Role of Operating Systems in Trusted AI
items.description: Panellist at CPDP 2026 on DMA Article 6(7) interoperability obligations, the tension between forced OS openness and GDPR-level privacy protections, hardware and software access risks, and whether a single interoperability standard can work across Apple, Google, and other platforms.
items.venue: Computers, Privacy & Data Protection Conference (CPDP2026), Brussels

items.title: Expert Workshop: Web Standards for Data Protection in the EU
items.description: Invited participation in the RegTech4AI expert workshop on Article 88b of the Omnibus proposal and a potential standardisation mandate for automated privacy signals. Discussion covered GPC adoption, the iOS/WebKit constraint on browser-level signals, and the policy boundary between targeting and attribution.
items.venue: RegTech4AI / Maastricht Law and Tech Lab, Brussels

items.title: Roundtable: Anonymisation at the Crossroads of EU Digital Regulations
items.description: Expert participation in a public roundtable on DMA Article 6(11) organised by Sophie Stalla-Bourdillon at VUB Brussels Privacy Hub. Discussion covered anonymisation of search data, singling out as the central test, how sessionisation and linkability enable re-identification, and the risk of incoherence between DMA and GDPR anonymisation standards.

rssMetadata.excerpt: Expert participation in VUB Brussels Privacy Hub roundtable on DMA Article 6(11) and anonymisation, examining singling out as the central re-identification test and the risk of diverging standards between DMA and GDPR.

items.title: Bridging Borders with Trust: PETs to Preserve Customer Control in Cross-Border Legal Conflict
items.description: Panel at the Privacy Symposium 2026 in Venice examining how privacy-enhancing technologies, particularly confidential computing and trusted execution environments, can reconcile cross-border data flows with data residency requirements and regulatory friction across jurisdictions.

rssMetadata.excerpt: Panel at Privacy Symposium 2026 Venice on how confidential computing and trusted execution environments can reconcile cross-border data flows with data residency requirements and digital sovereignty frameworks.

items.title: Data Protection Day 2026: Chasing Shadows
items.description: Moderated the Data Protection Day 2026 panel 'Chasing Shadows: Can regulation keep up as online tracking continues to transform?'. The panel debated whether the Digital Omnibus proposal modernises the ePrivacy rules on online tracking or erodes fundamental rights, and how standardised browser consent signals fit the GDPR's requirement for granular consent.
items.venue: EDPS and Council of Europe, Brussels
